newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says sees no need for int'l procurement pacts.
newsitem.headline: NTT says sees no need for int'l procurement pacts.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp president Junichiro Miyazu told a news conference on Wednesday that he sees no need for international procurement pacts.
"NTT's international purchases have been steadily increasing and our basic stance is to buy the best products at the cheapest price," Miyazu told a news conference.
He added that the market environment and types of purchases have changed since the Japanese government signed a pact with the United States on NTT's international purchases in the early 1980s.
The procurement pact, which sets guidelines for NTT's international purchases of equipment, expires in September and U.S. officials have been urging Japan to renew it.
"I feel it is useless to continue with the pact in the same format," he said, but he added it was up to the two governments to decide on the pact's future.

The pact was also cited by the U.S. Federal Telecommunications Commission earlier this month when it announced that it would not quickly grant NTT and Kokusai Denshin Denwa (KDD) U.S. international phone licences.
U.S. officials have also called on Japan to scrap a 20 percent ceiling on foreign ownership in NTT and KDD.
